subject: Weekly Leadership Pulse — OKR status, QBR materials & critical asks
messages:
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly Leadership Pulse — OKR status, QBR materials & critical asks

Team — sending the weekly pulse early to give folks time before the QBR dry run next Wed. Short summary (top-line then asks):

Wins (what moved forward this week):
- Inference runtime: shipped hotfix that cut 95th p99 latency for long-context jobs by ~18%. Impact measured in staging — safe to include as a win in the deck.
- Sales: Closed two mid-market deals flagged in last week’s pipe review (combined ARR ~$1.2M). Aditya has the postmortems for one win.
- Observability: Console traces now show token-level cost breakdown per-route — should help the finance ask in QBR.

Risks / Near-term blockers:
- Dedicated capacity provisioning for EU region is delayed (estimated 7 business days). If not resolved, we risk missing the EU latency target in the QBR OKR scorecard.
- One regression test failing intermittently in the quantized path (low frequency but blocks rollout of q4 config).

Asks (what I need from you before Wed dry run):
1) Markus — can you provide a 1-slide summary of the EU capacity mitigation plan + ETA for capacity commit? We need a concrete fallback to include in the QBR.
2) Laura — please sign off on the ‘customer outcomes’ slide. I drafted a short case study for Acme and attached metrics; need your storytelling edit.
3) Lauren — finance needs the token-cost delta table for the new batching policy (one-line summary in slide + CSV). I attached a CSV stub; can you confirm figures are final?
4) Aditya — pipeline slide: highlight the two closed deals and update ACV numbers.

Attachments: QBR-Pulse-Slides-v2.pdf (master slide deck, placeholders), OKR-Health-Table-20260322.csv (raw OKR numbers).

Quick ask on format: please reply inline with any redlines or upload slide edits to the Drive link below by EOD Tue so I can fold changes into the dry run.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bQBRFolderId

Thanks —
Maya
Maya Srinivasan
VP, Product & GTM Operations
Redwood Inference

> Team — sending the weekly pulse early to give folks time before the QBR dry run next Wed. Short summary (top-line then asks):
> 
> Wins (what moved forward this week):

> 
Thanks Maya — great framing. Small edits from my side:
- Customer outcomes: I tightened the Acme case study and added a short quote from their CPO (permission received).
- Slide ask: I can take the lead on the customer storytelling slide — will push an updated slide to the Drive by Tue noon.

Also: re the EU capacity risk, if we can't get firm commit by Tue EOD, I recommend we add an explicit mitigation note in the QBR: "Degraded EU throughput mitigated via routing to Dedicated EU partner pool until physical capacity is provisioned". That gives a clear stopgap.

I'll upload the edited slide and leave inline comments on the main deck.

Laura
Laura Bennett

Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly Leadership Pulse — OKR status, QBR materials & critical asks

On Mon, Mar 23, 2026 at 09:11 Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Maya — great framing. Small edits from my side:
> - Customer outcomes: I tightened the Acme case study...
> 
Quick follow-up from infra side. The EU capacity delay is due to a GPU allocation backlog at the provider (we have a partial allocation but not the full pool). Current estimates: 5–8 business days to reach committed throughput if we stick to the ordered hardware.

Proposed options (short):
- Short term (recommended): Route non-latency-critical traffic to the partner pool + enable autoscale burst for the next 2 weeks.
- Medium term: Re-allocate some reserved capacity from unused dev pools (will require approval from finance).

I'll prepare a 1-slide mitigation plan; pulling numbers from infra now. If we want the "explicit mitigation" language in the deck (Laura's suggestion), I support it.

Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly Leadership Pulse — OKR status, QBR materials & critical asks

Thanks for the fast turnaround, team — consolidating final asks and timeline so we have a single source for the dry run: 

Final checklist for Wed dry run (Mar 26, 10:00 AM PT):
- Markus: 1 mitigation slide + bullets with ETA (drop into Drive by 8:00 AM Wed).
- Laura: customer slide updated (accepted) — thanks; please annotate any final phrasing by Tue EOD if not already.
- Lauren: confirm token-cost delta numbers; if not final, flag which rows are estimates.
- Aditya: updated pipeline slide with ACV and close dates.

Deck notes: I merged Laura's edits and added a short "latency improvements" callout on slide 4 reflecting the hotfix. I also added a short appendix with OKR health table (see attached CSV).

Attachments uploaded: QBR-Pulse-Slides-v2.pdf (master for comments), OKR-Health-Table-20260322.csv
Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bQBRFolderId

If anything changes overnight, reply to this thread with the exact slide filename to avoid version conflict. Otherwise I'll finalize the deck at 8:30 AM Wed and circulate the dry-run invite.

Maya
